seo.title: Best Craft Beer Bars in Brno (2026) | tabiji.ai
seo.metaDescription: Discover the top 12 craft beer bars in Brno, Czech Republic. From cozy pubs to innovative brewpubs, find your perfect pint with our expert picks and local tips.

hero.h1: 12 Best Craft Beer Bars in Brno
hero.subtitle: Brno's craft beer scene is a vibrant and growing tapestry, offering everything from traditional Czech lagers with a twist to experimental IPAs and stouts from local microbreweries.

picks.name: Pivní Opice (Beer Monkey)
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Pivní Opice is a cornerstone of Brno's craft beer scene, boasting an impressive and ever-rotating selection of local and international brews across numerous taps. The cozy, brick-walled interior creates a perfect atmosphere for sampling, whether you're a seasoned enthusiast or new to craft beer. They often host tap takeovers and special events, making each visit unique.
picks.whatToOrder: A tasting flight (degustace) to sample several of their rotating taps, often featuring rare Czech IPAs or stouts.
picks.insiderTip: Check their online tap list before visiting, as their selection changes frequently. It can get busy, so consider an early evening visit for a more relaxed experience.
picks.redditQuote: "Pivní Opice is hands down my favorite in Brno. Always something new and exciting on tap, plus the staff really knows their stuff. You can't go wrong there."

picks.name: U Tří Kohoutů (At the Three Roosters)
picks.whyItMadeTheList: This popular brewpub offers a fantastic blend of traditional Czech hospitality and modern craft brewing. U Tří Kohoutů brews its own excellent beers on-site, ranging from classic lagers to more adventurous ales, all served fresh from the tank. The atmosphere is lively and inviting, perfect for both casual drinks and a full meal.
picks.whatToOrder: Try their 'Kohout 11' lager for a perfect local experience, or ask about their seasonal special brew. Pair it with their delicious nakládaný hermelín (pickled cheese).
picks.insiderTip: They have a lovely beer garden in the warmer months, which is a great spot to enjoy their fresh brews. Reservations are recommended for dinner, especially on weekends.
picks.redditQuote: "Love U Tří Kohoutů! Their own beers are consistently good, and the food is proper Czech pub grub. The atmosphere is always buzzing, really adds to the experience."

picks.name: Pivní Burza (Beer Exchange)
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Pivní Burza offers a unique and interactive craft beer experience where beer prices fluctuate based on demand, just like a stock exchange. With a large selection of Czech and international craft beers on tap, displayed on digital boards, it's a fun and engaging way to discover new brews. The excitement of watching prices drop (or rise!) adds a playful element to your evening.
picks.whatToOrder: Keep an eye on the screens for your favorite style when the price 'crashes', or try something completely new you might not usually splurge on.
picks.insiderTip: Go with a group and make a game out of predicting price changes. The 'market crash' event, usually once an hour, is when all prices temporarily plummet.
picks.redditQuote: "Pivní Burza is such a fun concept! I managed to snag a really good IPA for cheap when the market crashed. It's a great spot for groups to try different beers."

picks.name: Sklípek (The Cellar)
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Tucked away in the charming Veveří neighborhood, Sklípek lives up to its name with a cozy, cellar-like atmosphere. This intimate bar focuses on bringing lesser-known, high-quality craft beers from smaller Czech breweries to the forefront. It's a fantastic spot for those looking to explore unique, artisanal brews away from the main tourist paths.
picks.whatToOrder: Ask the knowledgeable staff for a recommendation based on your preferred style; they excel at introducing new and rare Czech craft beers.
picks.insiderTip: Due to its small size, Sklípek fills up quickly, especially on weekend evenings. It's ideal for a quiet conversation and serious beer tasting.
picks.redditQuote: "Sklípek is my hidden gem in Brno. Always a great selection of microbreweries you won't find elsewhere, and the staff are incredibly passionate about beer."

picks.name: Pivovar Hauskrecht
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Pivovar Hauskrecht is a modern brewery and restaurant offering its own range of meticulously crafted beers alongside a menu of hearty Czech dishes. The spacious interior combines industrial aesthetics with a warm, inviting feel, making it suitable for both casual visits and larger gatherings. Their beers are brewed with precision, often featuring both traditional and modern styles.
picks.whatToOrder: Their unfiltered lager is a must-try, showcasing the purity of Czech brewing. Pair it with their excellent guláš or svíčková.
picks.insiderTip: Located slightly outside the immediate city center, it's easily accessible by public transport (trams). It's a great option for a full evening out combining dinner and fresh beer.
picks.redditQuote: "Hauskrecht is a solid choice for good beer and food. Their own brews are consistently great, and the atmosphere is modern but still very welcoming."

picks.name: Na Stojáka (Standing Bar)
picks.whyItMadeTheList: As the name suggests, Na Stojáka is primarily a standing bar, emphasizing quick, high-quality beer served with minimal fuss. It's a bustling spot popular with locals, offering an excellent rotating selection of craft beers, often with a focus on smaller Czech breweries. It's the perfect place for a pre-dinner pint or a casual meeting with friends, enjoying the vibrant street-side atmosphere.
picks.whatToOrder: Any of their rotating taps – the selection changes daily. Grab a 'utopenec' (pickled sausage) or 'nakládaný hermelín' (pickled cheese) for a classic Czech pub snack.
picks.insiderTip: Embrace the standing experience; it's part of the charm and fosters easy conversation. Cash is often preferred, though cards are usually accepted.
picks.redditQuote: "Na Stojáka is legendary for a reason. Great beer, great vibe, and you always end up chatting with someone new. Definitely try the pickled cheese with your pint!"

picks.name: Pivnice U Čepů
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Pivnice U Čepů is a beloved local pub in the Veveří district, known for its extensive and carefully curated tap list. It successfully blends the feel of a traditional Czech pivnice with a modern appreciation for craft beer, offering both classic lagers and a diverse range of ales from various Czech microbreweries. The atmosphere is warm, friendly, and unpretentious.
picks.whatToOrder: Ask about their seasonal dark lager or a special IPA from a regional brewery, often displayed on their chalkboards.
picks.insiderTip: It's a great place to experience a genuine local pub atmosphere away from the busiest tourist areas. They often have good lunch specials too.
picks.redditQuote: "U Čepů is solid. Always a great selection of local craft beers and the atmosphere is exactly what you want from a neighborhood pub. Friendly staff too."

picks.name: Pivovar Poupě
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Pivovar Poupě is a newer addition to Brno's brewpub scene, quickly gaining a reputation for its innovative approach to brewing and its contemporary restaurant. They experiment with a wide range of styles, from crisp lagers to fruit-infused sours and robust stouts, all brewed on-site. The stylish, industrial-chic interior provides a comfortable setting for enjoying their creations.
picks.whatToOrder: Try their 'Poupě IPA' for a hoppy kick or their seasonal sour. Their food menu is equally creative and pairs well with their beers.
picks.insiderTip: While a bit further from the city center, it's worth the short tram ride for the quality of both the beer and food. They often have live music or special events.
picks.redditQuote: "Poupě is really impressing me lately. Their beers are super interesting, and the food is a step above typical pub fare. A great spot if you're looking for something a bit more modern."

picks.name: Zlatá Loď (Golden Ship)
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Zlatá Loď is a historic establishment that, while traditionally known for mainstream beers, has expanded its offerings to include a commendable selection of craft brews. It provides a classic Czech pub experience with a lively atmosphere and a mix of locals and visitors. Their commitment to offering quality craft options alongside their traditional staples makes it a versatile choice.
picks.whatToOrder: They often feature guest taps from smaller Czech craft breweries; ask the bar staff what's new or unique.
picks.insiderTip: It's centrally located and a good starting point for a beer crawl in the Old Town. Can get very busy, especially on weekends.
picks.redditQuote: "Zlatá Loď might look traditional but they actually have some decent craft taps now. Good spot if you're with a mixed group and some want craft, others just a Pilsner."

picks.name: Pivní Jarmark (Beer Fair)
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Pivní Jarmark functions as both a well-stocked craft beer bottle shop and a cozy bar with several taps. It's a paradise for beer lovers looking to discover new bottles from around the world or enjoy a fresh pint in a relaxed setting. The knowledgeable staff are always on hand to help navigate their extensive selection, making it a great place to find a unique souvenir or a new favorite brew.
picks.whatToOrder: Choose from their rotating tap list, or select a bottle from their vast collection to drink on-site (for a small corkage fee) or take home.
picks.insiderTip: If you find a beer you love on tap, check their fridges – you might be able to buy a bottle to enjoy later. They also host occasional tasting events.
picks.redditQuote: "Pivní Jarmark is my go-to for grabbing bottles to take home, but their tap selection is always solid too. The staff are super helpful if you're trying to find something specific."

picks.name: Bar, který neexistuje (The Bar That Doesn't Exist)
picks.whyItMadeTheList: While renowned for its innovative cocktail program, Bar, který neexistuje also boasts a surprisingly thoughtful selection of craft beers, often featuring premium local and international brews. This sophisticated bar offers a stylish, dimly lit ambiance perfect for an upscale evening. It's an excellent choice if you're with friends who prefer cocktails but you still want a quality craft beer.
picks.whatToOrder: Ask about their current craft beer taps; they often carry unique selections from smaller, high-quality breweries. Don't overlook their famous cocktails either!
picks.insiderTip: Make a reservation if you plan to visit on a weekend, as it gets very busy. It's a great spot for a date night or a special occasion.
picks.redditQuote: "Most people go for cocktails, but Bar, který neexistuje actually has a really respectable craft beer list. Perfect when I want a good beer and my partner wants a fancy drink."

picks.name: Výčep Na Květné
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Výčep Na Květné is a charming, unpretentious local pub focusing on quality Czech craft beer. It offers a rotating selection of taps from smaller regional breweries, ensuring a fresh and diverse experience with each visit. The atmosphere is laid-back and friendly, making it an ideal spot to unwind and enjoy excellent beer in a genuine local setting.
picks.whatToOrder: Their pilsner-style craft lagers are always crisp and well-executed, but also keep an eye out for their special dark ales.
picks.insiderTip: This bar is a bit off the main drag but well worth the short walk from the city center. It's a perfect place to feel like a local.
picks.redditQuote: "Discovered Výčep Na Květné by accident and it's now a regular stop. Great selection of lesser-known Czech craft beers and a really chill vibe. Highly recommend."

faq.question: What is the average price of a craft beer in Brno?
faq.answer: The price of a 0.5L (pint) of craft beer in Brno typically ranges from 80 CZK to 150 CZK ($3.50-$6.50), depending on the brewery, style, and venue. Imported craft beers or special releases might be slightly higher. This is generally more affordable than in many Western European cities.

faq.question: Are craft beer bars in Brno English-friendly?
faq.answer: Most popular craft beer bars in Brno, especially those in the city center or catering to a younger crowd, will have staff who speak English. Menus often have English translations or can be explained by the staff, making it easy for international visitors to enjoy the scene.

faq.question: Do Brno craft beer bars serve food?
faq.answer: Many craft beer bars in Brno, particularly brewpubs, offer a full food menu featuring traditional Czech cuisine and pub snacks. Even bars primarily focused on beer often have small bites like nakládaný hermelín (pickled cheese) or utopenec (pickled sausage) that pair perfectly with beer.

faq.question: What kind of craft beer styles are popular in Brno?
faq.answer: While traditional Czech lagers (especially Pilsner-style) remain popular, Brno's craft scene embraces a wide range of styles. You'll find excellent Czech-made IPAs, pale ales, stouts, porters, sours, and seasonal specialties. Local brewers are increasingly experimenting with modern styles while honoring Czech brewing heritage.

faq.question: Is it customary to tip in craft beer bars in Brno?
faq.answer: Tipping is customary in Brno, usually by rounding up the bill or adding 5-10% for good service, especially if you're impressed with the staff's knowledge and recommendations. You can simply tell the server the total amount you wish to pay, including the tip, when they present the bill.

faq.question: What's the best way to get around Brno to visit different bars?
faq.answer: Brno has an excellent public transport system of trams and buses, making it easy to hop between different neighborhoods. Many of the best craft beer bars are concentrated in the city center and Veveří, making them easily walkable. Taxis and ride-sharing services are also readily available for longer distances or late nights.

methodology: Our selection of Brno's best craft beer bars is based on extensive local research, expert recommendations, and analysis of online reviews from popular travel and food platforms. We prioritize venues known for diverse tap lists, quality brews, unique atmospheres, and excellent service, ensuring both local gems and well-loved institutions are represented.
